title: OverflowTabs
wrapsNative: MonarchTabs, which scrolls sideways in a ScrollView when its tabs do not fit
summary: A recipe, not a component: a tab strip with more tabs than fit. MonarchTabs already scrolls sideways and brings the selected tab into view; when the extra tabs should sit in a More menu, compose MonarchTabs with a Menu.
whenToUse: For the sections of a record or a page when there are more of them than fit across a phone, for example six sections of a project.
whenNotToUse: For the top-level destinations of an app use TabView (see bottom-tab-bar), which has its own More tab. For two to four sections use MonarchTabs alone or a segmented Picker.
api: MonarchTabs.init(_ label: String, selection: Binding<Value>, items: [MonarchTabsItem<Value>], variant: MonarchTabsVariant = .line)
Menu(content: () -> some View, label: () -> some View)
Picker(_ title: String, selection: Binding<Value>, content: () -> some View).pickerStyle(.inline)

states.name: scrolling
states.description: MonarchTabs on its own: the strip scrolls sideways and a newly selected tab scrolls into view.

states.name: more menu
states.description: The first tabs are in the strip and the rest in a More menu; the menu's label shows the chosen tab's name when one of its tabs is selected.

states.name: selected in the menu
states.description: No tab in the strip is marked; the More button carries the name, and the Picker in the menu marks it with a checkmark.

appearance: The strip is MonarchTabs (line or pill) and the More button a ghost Monarch button; the menu is the system's.
platformNotes: The web OverflowTabs measures the strip and moves the last tabs into a More menu as the width shrinks. On iOS MonarchTabs scrolls instead, which keeps every tab one swipe away and needs no measuring; the More menu recipe splits at a fixed count chosen by the app. The web's TabsContent panels are the app's own views switched on the selection. Android uses the scrolling tab row of Material 3 natively.
accessibility: MonarchTabs is a tab bar with each tab a button with the selected trait; VoiceOver reaches scrolled-off tabs by swiping.
The More button names the selected overflow tab, so the selection is not hidden in the menu; the inline Picker in the menu reads which tab is selected.
Every tab and the More button have a touch target of at least 44 points.
edgeCases: With the More menu, choose the split so the strip fits at the largest text size, or let the strip scroll as well.
Tab values must be unique across the strip and the menu.

examples.title: Wide
examples.template:
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {
    // The tabs scroll sideways when they do not fit, so every tab of the web example is in the strip.
    MonarchTabs(
        {{label}},
        selection: $section,
        items: [
            MonarchTabsItem({{tabs.0.label}}, value: {{tabs.0.value}}),
            MonarchTabsItem({{tabs.1.label}}, value: {{tabs.1.value}}, count: "{{tabs.1.count|raw}}", countTone: {{tabs.1.countTone|tone}}),
            MonarchTabsItem({{tabs.2.label}}, value: {{tabs.2.value}}),
            MonarchTabsItem({{tabs.3.label}}, value: {{tabs.3.value}}),
            MonarchTabsItem({{tabs.4.label}}, value: {{tabs.4.value}}),
            MonarchTabsItem({{tabs.5.label}}, value: {{tabs.5.value}}, isDisabled: {{tabs.5.disabled}}),
            MonarchTabsItem({{tabs.6.label}}, value: {{tabs.6.value}}),
            MonarchTabsItem({{tabs.7.label}}, value: {{tabs.7.value}}),
        ]
    )
    Text("\(titles[section] ?? "") content")
}
examples.setupTemplate:
@State private var section = {{selected}}
private let titles = [{{tabs.0.value}}: {{tabs.0.label}}, {{tabs.1.value}}: {{tabs.1.label}}, {{tabs.2.value}}: {{tabs.2.label}}, {{tabs.3.value}}: {{tabs.3.label}}, {{tabs.4.value}}: {{tabs.4.label}}, {{tabs.5.value}}: {{tabs.5.label}}, {{tabs.6.value}}: {{tabs.6.label}}, {{tabs.7.value}}: {{tabs.7.label}}]
examples.setup:
@State private var section = "overview"
private let titles = ["overview": "Overview", "activity": "Activity", "files": "Files", "members": "Members", "integrations": "Integrations", "billing": "Billing", "audit": "Audit log", "settings": "Settings"]
examples.code:
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {
    // The tabs scroll sideways when they do not fit, so every tab of the web example is in the strip.
    MonarchTabs(
        "Workspace sections",
        selection: $section,
        items: [
            MonarchTabsItem("Overview", value: "overview"),
            MonarchTabsItem("Activity", value: "activity", count: "4", countTone: .accent),
            MonarchTabsItem("Files", value: "files"),
            MonarchTabsItem("Members", value: "members"),
            MonarchTabsItem("Integrations", value: "integrations"),
            MonarchTabsItem("Billing", value: "billing", isDisabled: true),
            MonarchTabsItem("Audit log", value: "audit"),
            MonarchTabsItem("Settings", value: "settings"),
        ]
    )
    Text("\(titles[section] ?? "") content")
}

examples.title: The last tabs in a More menu
examples.setup:
@State private var section = "overview"
private let sections = [
    MonarchTabsItem("Overview", value: "overview"),
    MonarchTabsItem("Activity", value: "activity", count: "3"),
    MonarchTabsItem("Members", value: "members"),
    MonarchTabsItem("Billing", value: "billing"),
    MonarchTabsItem("Security", value: "security"),
    MonarchTabsItem("Audit log", value: "audit"),
]

parityExceptions.reason: The web example is wide and shows all eight tabs at once; a 354-point phone column shows the first four and the strip scrolls sideways to the rest (every tab of the web example is in it, none is moved into a menu). A width limit of the device, not a layout change.
parityExceptions.convention: HIG: a tab strip that does not fit scrolls
